result:
Clean typecheck, all 617 tests still pass.

Summary of what I implemented, per ADR 0005:

- `src/config/constants.ts`: `ORG_SLUG_HOLD_DAYS = 30`.
- `src/schemas/organization.ts`: `renameOrganizationSlugSchema` / `RenameOrganizationSlugInput`.
- `src/server/services/organization-service.ts`: `renameOrganizationSlug` — permission-checked, no-op on same slug, validates shape via `assertValidSlug`, refuses (never suffixes) unavailable slugs with `InvalidSlugError`, retires the old slug, and emits `organization.slug_changed` on behalf of the actor.
- `src/types/event.ts`: new `organization.slug_changed` event (`EventEnvelope & { from, to }`).
- `src/types/activity.ts` + `src/schemas/activity.ts` + `activity-labels.ts`: new `organization.slug_changed` audit action wired everywhere `ActivityAction` is accepted.
- `src/server/services/activity-service.ts`: subscribes to the new event and records the audit row (subject `organization`, metadata `{ from, to }`), matching the existing event→audit pattern.
- New `organization_retired_slugs` table (schema + migration fallback) that records each retired slug with its own `retiredAt`, so chained renames keep independent holds.
- `organization-repository.ts`: `findOrgBySlug` now falls back to an unexpired retired slug (fixing resolution everywhere — session layer, dashboard layout, tenant context, since they all funnel through this one function); `listTakenOrgSlugs` now treats actively-held retired slugs as taken too, so org creation's suffixing never collides with a hold; new `isSlugCurrentForAnotherOrg` / `isSlugRetiredByAnotherOrg` availability checks; new `renameOrgSlug` writer that un-retires a self-held target slug and retires the slug being replaced.

Verified with a scratch test (removed after use) covering no-op, successful rename, old-slug resolution, cross-org rejection of both current and retired slugs, permission denial, and the self-reclaim chain — all behaved per the ADR.
